verdict.rationale: First-party docs describe a deep literature review that starts from an open-ended research goal, plans its own searches, follows citations and key authors, and stops only when new searches stop finding relevant papers, then produces a ranked list with a written synthesis. That is an autonomous multi-step investigation rather than a single pass. Community reports of 3–6 minute runs, an exhaustiveness/discovery-progress readout, and 'comprehensive understanding' fit this iterative process, though some users noted missed gray literature and repetitive results. Missing for 10: independent hands-on description of the agent's actual step-by-step planning (corroboration is indirect, via latency and progress indicators), and evidence of investigation beyond literature search (e.g., multi-step analysis outside paper discovery).
